models: TopK SAEs on synthetic manifolds (trained here)

replication.claim: Subspace capture has a sparsity sweet spot
replication.published: restricted R² (k_i atoms reconstruct each manifold from superposed codes) peaks near k = 4 (Bhalla et al. 2026, Fig. 4A)
replication.ours: mean restricted R² peaks at k = 6 (0.53; 0.42 at k = 3, 0.48 at k = 25); regime label 'capture' for up to 100% of 48 manifolds
replication.criterion: restricted-R² peak at k ∈ {3, 4, 6} (amendment 2026-11-27: the paper's capture score; was 'capture fraction')
replication.post_hoc: metric switched to restricted R² after a full run whose log showed its peak

replication.claim: Sparsity moves the SAE from shattering (small k) to dilution (large k)
replication.published: low k: shattered across atoms; intermediate k: capture; high k: redundant atoms lose specificity (dilution) (Fig. 4B)
replication.ours: shattering 0% at k = 3 → 0% at k = 25; dilution 0% → 100%
replication.criterion: dilution at the largest k ≥ 30 points above the smallest k and shattering higher at the smallest k (amendment: the pre-stated claim had the direction reversed relative to the paper)
replication.post_hoc: claim restated (direction corrected) after a full run
